overview: Monday's session was defined by one headline: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated founder Jensen Huang as President and CEO, effective immediately, after concluding the reinstatement posed no national security risk. The move triggered the strongest one-day equity rally in months — the Nasdaq surged 6.5%, the S&P 500 jumped 4.8%, and Nvidia shares climbed approximately 31%. The dollar eased from 19-month highs as the risk-on sentiment reduced safe-haven demand, and gold reversed sharply higher. COMEX gold settled 3.90% higher at $3,649.20, snapping a ten-session losing streak and recovering from a 14-month low reached last week. Spot gold closed near $3,650 per ounce. Silver gained approximately 3.6% to $43. Platinum rose 2.7% to $1,330; palladium edged up to $900. The rebound came as December rate-hike odds eased slightly to around 90% from 99% and the October PCE inflation report is due Wednesday. Despite the equity rally, oil moved in the opposite direction: Brent crude fell 3.46% to $89.37 per barrel — its lowest close since August — as Libya reopened its Sharara pipeline and Middle East crude flows continued to recover. WTI settled at $80.17. OPEC+ ministers meet on November 29 to decide 2027 output policy.

The November 27 deadline for China's US-specific export-control suspension on gallium, germanium and antimony is now 3 days away with no extension announced. COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey collapsed on Sunday over fossil fuel phase-out wording, eliminating the last major multilateral venue before the deadline. Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have reached the highest levels since the conflict began, with 6 tankers struck in the past week. Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched a missile-and-drone assault on US military positions in Bahrain over the weekend; Houthis separately attacked a Saudi oil refinery. Despite these escalations, Middle East crude export flows are recovering and traffic through the Strait, though still 65% below pre-conflict levels, is stabilising. LME base metals were mixed: copper recovered approximately 2.4% to $5.65 per pound as the dollar eased; nickel rose slightly to $15,400; zinc was flat at $3,500; tin edged to $41,100. Grains were modestly higher: December corn 435½ cents (up 1 cent), December SRW wheat 577¾ cents (up 3½ cents), January soybeans 1,228¾ cents (up 8 cents). Bitcoin spiked to nearly $64,000 intraday on the Nvidia-driven rally but pulled back to approximately $61,200 by evening — the Fear and Greed Index remains at 11 (Extreme Fear). Ethereum touched $1,825 before settling near $1,730. LNG JKM held near $31 per MMBtu as winter demand supports.

watchItems.title: November 27 gallium, germanium and antimony deadline now 3 days away — COP31 collapsed, no diplomatic venue remains
watchItems.text: The November 27 deadline for China's US-specific export-control suspension on gallium, germanium and antimony is now 3 days away with no extension announced. COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey collapsed on Sunday over fossil fuel phase-out wording, eliminating the last major multilateral venue before the deadline. The G20 Finance Ministers meeting in Atlanta (October 31–November 1) had already ended without consensus on critical minerals. China produces approximately 99% of global gallium, 60–80% of germanium, and close to half of mined antimony. Gallium holds near $2,100 per kilogram outside China versus approximately $460 domestically — a roughly 4.5x premium. Alcoa's Wagerup gallium refinery has taken FID but is not yet producing. If the bans resume on Thursday, Western semiconductor and defence supply chains face renewed disruption.

watchItems.title: Oil falls to August lows as Libya reopens Sharara pipeline and Middle East flows recover — OPEC+ meets November 29
watchItems.text: Brent crude fell 3.46% on Monday to $89.37 per barrel — its lowest close since August — as two supply-side developments overwhelmed ongoing geopolitical concerns. Libya's NOC confirmed crude from the Sharara pipeline is reaching storage at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, adding significant supply. Middle East crude flows are recovering toward pre-war levels despite attacks at the highest rate since the conflict began. WTI settled at $80.17. JPMorgan expects oil futures to fall into the high $70s in the first half of 2027. OPEC+ ministers meet on November 29 to decide 2027 output policy — the market is watching whether the group will commit to output restraint amid weakening prices and surplus forecasts.

watchItems.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang — Nasdaq surges 6.5%, dollar eases, gold snaps 10-session losing streak
watchItems.text: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated founder Jensen Huang as President and CEO effective immediately, triggering the strongest one-day equity rally in months. The Nasdaq surged 6.5%, the S&P 500 jumped 4.8%, and Nvidia shares climbed approximately 31% to $161.57. The board concluded the reinstatement posed no national security risk, though an independent investigation into foreign intelligence ties will continue to its conclusion. The company is also forming a National Security and Export Control Committee and appointing a new Chief Compliance Officer. The rally eased the dollar from 19-month highs, allowing gold to snap its ten-session losing streak with a 3.9% surge to $3,650 — a critical technical reversal. The question is whether this risk-on impulse sustains or was a one-day event.

watchItems.title: Hormuz attacks at highest rate since conflict began — Iran strikes Bahrain, Houthis hit Saudi refinery
watchItems.text: Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have reached the highest levels since the conflict began, with 6 tankers struck in the past week. JMIC continues to rate the threat as severe. Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched a missile-and-drone assault on US military positions in Bahrain over the weekend, and Houthis separately attacked a Saudi Arabian oil refinery — a significant escalation in the regional conflict. Combined Hormuz traffic remains approximately 65% below pre-conflict levels, with about 490 vessels waiting outside the Strait. Despite the sustained attacks, the paradox deepens: Middle East crude export flows are recovering toward pre-war levels, and the oil price fell 3.5% on Monday. Three US carrier strike groups remain in the Gulf.

desk.name: Gold
desk.m: Snapped 10-session losing streak · COMEX settle $3,649 +3.90% · dollar eased from 19-month high · Dec hike odds ~90% (down from 99%) · Oct PCE due Wed
desk.sum: Gold reversed sharply higher on Monday, with COMEX December futures settling 3.90% higher at $3,649.20 — snapping a ten-session losing streak that had pushed the metal to a 14-month low. Spot gold closed near $3,650 per ounce. The catalyst was Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO, which triggered a massive equity rally (Nasdaq +6.5%) and eased the dollar from 19-month highs. The dollar retreat was the proximate driver for gold, as rate-hike expectations simultaneously softened: December 25bp odds eased to approximately 90% from 99%, with 50bp expectations declining further. The October PCE inflation report due Wednesday will be the next swing factor. Key resistance at $3,700; support at $3,600.

desk.name: Silver
desk.m: Rebounded from 14-month low · gold-silver ratio ~85 · COMEX Dec futures +3.7% · dollar easing supports · higher beta amplified gains
desk.sum: Silver surged approximately 3.6% to $43 per ounce on Monday, rebounding from its own 14-month low as the dollar eased from 19-month highs. Silver's higher beta to gold amplified the move — COMEX December futures were up 3.7% at $42.59 in pre-market trading and extended gains through the US session. The gold-silver ratio held near 85. The Nvidia-driven equity rally and dollar retreat provided dual support for silver's precious-industrial profile. The rebound was technically significant, reclaiming the $42 level after last week's break below it. Key resistance at $44; support at $41.

desk.name: Oil
desk.m: WTI $80.17 · lowest since Aug · Libya Sharara pipeline reopens · ME flows recovering · JPMorgan sees high $70s H1 2027 · OPEC+ meets Nov 29
desk.sum: Brent crude fell 3.46% on Monday to $89.37 per barrel — its lowest close since August and its third consecutive weekly decline. WTI settled at $80.17. The sell-off was driven by two supply-side developments: Libya reopened its Sharara pipeline, with crude reaching storage at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, and Middle East crude flows continued to recover toward pre-war levels despite attacks at the highest rate since the conflict began. JPMorgan expects oil futures to fall into the high $70s in H1 2027. OPEC+ ministers meet on November 29 to decide 2027 output policy. The oil sell-off occurred despite a massive equity rally driven by Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang, underscoring that supply fundamentals are dominating crude sentiment.
desk.src: Nation Thailand · Reuters · RTE · Trading Economics

desk.name: Copper
desk.m: LME ~$12,450/t · recovered as dollar eased · still down ~16% from Sept record · Yangshan premium record $360 · 2027 TC benchmark may go negative
desk.sum: Copper recovered approximately 2.4% to $5.65 per pound (approximately $12,450 per tonne LME) on Monday as the dollar eased from 19-month highs following Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang. The rebound came after copper fell to its lowest level since April earlier this month amid the AI-driven equity sell-off. The Yangshan import premium hit a record $360 per tonne on Friday, and Chinese physical demand remains robust. SHFE copper stocks fell 18% in the week to November 14 to a near three-year low. A Reuters poll projects the 2027 treatment charge benchmark may turn negative for the first time. Copper remains approximately 16% below its September record of $14,875 per tonne.

desk.name: Coal
desk.m: Up ~40% YTD · held steady again · winter demand · LNG supply crisis continues · oil slide negative but energy substitution supports · OPEC+ Nov 29
desk.sum: Newcastle coal held at $150 per tonne on Monday, continuing to defy broader commodity moves as winter demand and the Hormuz-driven LNG supply crisis sustain the thermal fuel bid. Coal is up approximately 40% year to date. Monday's oil sell-off to $89.37 is modestly negative for coal (as cheaper oil reduces relative coal competitiveness), but the LNG supply crisis and coal-to-gas substitution dynamics provide a structural floor through winter. QatarEnergy's force majeure continues through at least end-December 2026. COP31 climate talks collapsed on Sunday without agreement on fossil fuel phase-out timelines.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.m: Rebounded with gold · dollar easing supportive · South African supply constrained · hydrogen demand structural · recovered from 14-month low zone
desk.sum: Platinum rose approximately 2.7% to $1,330 per ounce on Monday, rebounding with the broader precious metals complex as the dollar eased from 19-month highs. The recovery was driven by the same risk-on shift that pushed gold up 3.9% — Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang triggered an equity rally and dollar retreat. South African mine supply remains constrained by ongoing power issues. Hydrogen electrolysis demand provides structural long-term support. The rebound reclaimed the $1,300 level after last week's break below it. Key resistance at $1,350; support at $1,295.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.m: Reclaimed $900 · still near 2018 lows · EV transition headwind dominant · dollar easing marginal support · down ~35% YoY
desk.sum: Palladium edged up 0.6% to approximately $900 per ounce on Monday, reclaiming the psychologically significant $900 level as the dollar eased from 19-month highs. The recovery was modest compared to gold and silver — palladium's structural headwind from the EV transition (battery EVs require no catalytic converter) continues to cap rallies. Down approximately 35% year-over-year. Tight South African mine supply offers limited support. The $900 level is key: a sustained hold above it would signal consolidation, while a renewed break below opens the $870–$880 support zone.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: Attacks at highest rate since conflict began · 6 tankers hit in past week · IRGC struck US positions in Bahrain · Houthis hit Saudi refinery · traffic 65% below pre-conflict · JMIC: SEVERE · 3 carriers in Gulf
desk.sum: Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have reached the highest levels since the conflict began, with 6 tankers struck in the past week. JMIC continues to rate the threat as severe with further deliberate attacks highly likely. In a significant escalation over the weekend, Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched a missile-and-drone assault on US military positions in Bahrain, and Houthis attacked a Saudi Arabian oil refinery. Combined Hormuz traffic remains approximately 65% below pre-conflict levels, with about 490 vessels waiting outside the Strait. The deepening paradox: despite attacks at record levels, Middle East crude export flows are recovering toward pre-war levels — Brent fell 3.5% on Monday on the supply improvement. Three US carrier strike groups remain in the Gulf. OPEC+ ministers meet November 29.

desk.name: Corn
desk.m: Dec front-month · up 1¢ from Fri · dollar easing modestly supportive · Black Sea disruption ongoing · South American planting favourable · export commitments down 28% YoY
desk.sum: December corn settled at 435½ cents per bushel on Monday, up 1 cent as the dollar eased from 19-month highs following the Nvidia-driven equity rally. The modest gain came as bargain buying emerged after last week's decline. US corn export commitments remain down approximately 28% year-over-year. The stronger dollar has been a persistent headwind for US export competitiveness. South American planting continues under generally favourable conditions. Black Sea maritime disruption remains a potential support factor for US exports, though the conflict premium has faded from grain markets. Key support at 430 cents.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.m: Dec SRW · up 3½¢ · HRW $6.37½ mixed · dollar easing supportive · Black Sea disruption ongoing · export commitments down 30% YoY
desk.sum: December SRW wheat settled at 577¾ cents per bushel on Monday, up 3½ cents. HRW wheat was mixed at $6.37½. The modest gains came as the dollar eased from 19-month highs and soybean and meal strength limited selling pressure. US wheat export commitments remain down approximately 30% year-over-year. SovEcon's Russian wheat export estimate of 36 million tonnes — below the USDA's forecast — provides structural support. Black Sea disruption from earlier Ukrainian naval drone strikes continues to affect grain export routes. The dollar remains the dominant variable for US grain competitiveness.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.m: January front-month ~$12.29 · up 8¢ · meal strength drove gains · soybean oil weak at 8-month low · export commitments up 80% YoY · dollar easing supportive
desk.sum: January soybeans rose 8 cents to 1,228¾ cents per bushel on Monday, led higher by soybean meal strength. March soybean meal rallied $4.40 to $345.20 — a four-week high — on short covering and bargain hunting. Soybean oil was weak, however, falling 47 points to 60.05 cents — an eight-month low — pressured by the oil slide. US soybean export commitments are up approximately 80% year-over-year, the strongest among the grain complex. The dollar easing from 19-month highs following the Nvidia-driven rally provided additional support. South American supplies remain competitive at current exchange rates.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.m: ETH $1,730 · spiked to $63,888 intraday on Nvidia rally then pulled back · Fear & Greed 11 (Extreme Fear) · spot ETF outflows ~$1.24B last week · Dec hike odds eased to ~90%
desk.sum: Bitcoin spiked to approximately $63,888 intraday on Monday as the Nvidia-driven equity rally spilled into crypto, but the gains faded through the evening session, with BTC settling near $61,200 — up roughly 0.5% from Sunday. Ethereum touched $1,825 before pulling back to approximately $1,730. The intraday volatility underscores crypto's sensitivity to tech sentiment — the Nvidia reinstatement triggered a brief risk-on impulse that failed to sustain. The Fear and Greed Index remains at 11 (Extreme Fear). Spot Bitcoin ETF outflows were approximately $1.24 billion last week (November 16–20), the third consecutive week exceeding $1 billion. The key test is whether Bitcoin can hold above $60,000 as equities attempt to build on Monday's rally.

desk.name: LNG
desk.m: JKM Dec contract ~$31 · TTF ~$30 · HH ~$3.20 · QatarEnergy FM continues · EU storage ~71% — 20% below 5Y avg · oil slide may ease LNG floor slightly
desk.sum: The Asian LNG spot JKM December contract holds near $31 per MMBtu, firming as winter demand intensifies. TTF sits near $30 per MMBtu; Henry Hub near $3.20. EU gas storage at approximately 71% is roughly 20% below the five-year average heading into winter. QatarEnergy's force majeure extends through at least end-December 2026. The JKM December contract saw record activity in the week to November 18 as buyers locked in winter supply. Monday's oil sell-off to $89.37 may ease the LNG cost floor slightly, but the structural supply deficit from Hormuz-related disruption dominates. US LNG export feedgas remains near records.
desk.src: S&P Global Platts · Global LNG Hub · JOGMEC

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.m: FOB Kuwait ~$765 · Hormuz attacks highest since conflict began · 3 days to Nov 27 deadline · oil slide eases sulfur production dynamics slightly · 3 US carriers in Gulf
desk.sum: Sulfur remains elevated at approximately $1,200 per tonne CFR Southeast Asia. Hormuz attacks have reached the highest levels since the conflict began, though the paradox is that Middle East crude flows — and by extension sulfur supply logistics — are partially recovering. FOB Kuwait holds near $765 (KPC). Monday's oil slide to $89.37 modestly eases the petroleum-sulfur production dynamic. The November 27 export-control deadline is 3 days away with no extension announced. COP31 collapsed on Sunday, eliminating the last multilateral venue before the deadline.

desk.name: Potash
desk.m: BPC India $383 CFR · China benchmark ~$348 · grain prices stabilising · oil slide reduces input costs slightly · Black Sea disruption adds logistics risk
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds at approximately $358 per tonne. BPC's India contract remains approximately $25 above China's 2026 benchmark at $383 per tonne CFR. Monday's modest gains in corn and wheat, along with soybean meal strength, are marginally supportive for fertiliser demand sentiment after last week's weakness. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions. The oil slide to $89.37 modestly reduces potash production input costs. Black Sea disruption continues to add logistics risk to potash trade routes from the region.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.m: 3 days to Nov 27 deadline · Rotterdam $18,300–19,000/t · prices stabilised after Oct sell-off · no progress from any diplomatic channel · COP31 collapse removes last venue
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) holds near ¥92,000 per tonne, having stabilised after the sharp decline from ¥105,000 in early October. Overseas antimony sits at approximately $18,300–19,000 per tonne in Rotterdam. The November 27 deadline is now 3 days away with no extension announced. COP31 climate talks collapsed on Sunday, removing the last major multilateral venue before the deadline. Market participants continue to price in ban resumption. If the deadline passes without extension, overseas prices could spike further. China produces close to half of global mined antimony.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.m: Up >130% since early 2025 · 3 days to Nov 27 deadline · China domestic Ga ~$460/kg · COP31 collapse removes last venue · ban resumption increasingly priced in
desk.sum: Gallium holds near $2,100 per kilogram outside China, with Chinese domestic gallium at approximately $460 per kilogram — a roughly 4.5x premium. The November 27 deadline is now 3 days away with no extension announced. COP31 climate talks collapsed on Sunday in Antalya, removing the last major multilateral venue before the deadline. China produces approximately 99% of global gallium and 60–80% of germanium. The underlying licensing regimes remain in force during the suspension. Alcoa's Wagerup gallium refinery has taken FID but is not yet producing. Ban resumption is increasingly priced in.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.m: Steady at $5.30 · upstream tightness · VRFB adoption timeline uncertain · China-Russia-SA control 90%+ · Nov 27 deadline 3 days
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) holds at approximately $5.30 per pound in Europe, supported by persistent upstream tightness. The November 27 deadline, now 3 days away, affects the broader critical minerals complex. COP31 climate talks collapsed on Sunday with no agreement on fossil fuel phase-out, removing any potential last-minute diplomatic opening. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage, but large-scale adoption timing remains uncertain. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.m: Eased from $5,294 · Ivory Coast mid-crop may fall 42–50% YoY · ICE stocks at 2.5-year high · S&P GSCI cutting cocoa weighting · $5,000 support intact
desk.sum: ICE cocoa has eased toward $5,200 per tonne, pulling back from $5,294 at Friday's close. The market is caught between competing forces: Ivory Coast's Sodexam projects 2026/27 output down 21–25% due to El Niño, and Reuters sources suggest the mid-crop could fall 42–50% year-on-year to 300,000–350,000 tonnes. Against this, ICE warehouse inventories sit at a 2.5-year high of approximately 3.8 million bags, and both the S&P GSCI and Bloomberg Commodity Index plan to reduce cocoa weighting. The $5,000 level has held as strong psychological support. Chocolate demand remains subdued at current price levels.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.m: Continued gradual decline · Rotterdam $16–17/lb · DRC logistics disruption ongoing · NMC-to-LFP shift structural headwind · dollar easing marginal positive
desk.sum: Cobalt is estimated near $32,500 per tonne, continuing a gradual decline. Rotterdam standard-grade cobalt metal sits at $16–17 per pound. The DRC bridge collapse continues to have secondary effects on cobalt logistics, with alternative routes adding time and cost. The NMC-to-LFP battery chemistry shift weighs on the structural demand outlook. Monday's dollar easing from 19-month highs is a marginal positive, but the market remains in structural surplus. The CME Group noted cobalt is experiencing structural shifts from the last cycle top.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.m: Continued drift lower from ¥90,000 · structural oversupply persists · Goldman: 444k t global surplus by 2028 · November destocking continues
desk.sum: Chinese lithium carbonate continues to drift lower toward ¥88,000 per tonne, extending the decline from ¥90,000 earlier in November. Structural oversupply remains the dominant theme, with Goldman Sachs projecting a 444,000-tonne global surplus by 2028. SMM data shows sustained monthly destocking in November. The EU's plan to cap Chinese EV imports at 350,000 units per year adds a demand headwind. Supply ramp-ups in Australia and South America continue to outpace demand growth. The ¥85,000 zone represents next major support.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.m: $2.55/kg · SE Asia supply tight · fungal blight ongoing · oil slide reduces synthetic rubber costs · auto demand solid
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades near $2,550 per tonne ($2.55/kg), range-bound. Southeast Asian supply remains tight, with Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia — producing 70% of global latex — still affected by Pestalotiopsis fungal leaf blight. Monday's oil slide to $89.37 reduces synthetic rubber production costs, tilting the balance slightly away from natural rubber compared to last week when oil was above $92. Auto-sector demand remains solid, supported by replacement-tyre cycles. The dollar easing from 19-month highs provides marginal support.

desk.name: Uranium
desk.m: Spot held near $90 · term price $98/lb near record · IAEA: 78 reactors under construction · miners sliding while prices hold · AI demand structural
desk.sum: Uranium spot holds near $90 per pound U₃O₈, with long-term contract prices at $98 per pound — approaching the $100 milestone. Despite spot prices holding above $90 for most of November, uranium miners (URNM ETF) have continued to slide, reflecting rate sensitivity, contract-price lag and ETF-driven selling. The IAEA counts 78 reactors under construction worldwide. Kazatomprom reported 25% year-on-year sales turnover growth in Q3 with a 17% rise in average realized prices. AI data-centre power demand remains a structural driver, with Meta, Amazon and Microsoft having signed nuclear power agreements.

desk.name: Rare Earths
desk.m: Pr-Nd prices on the rise per SMM Nov 23 · ex-China NdPr below $110/kg · Nov 27 deadline 3 days · downstream demand sluggish
desk.sum: Neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) oxide has risen slightly to approximately $72 per kilogram domestically in China. SMM reported on November 23 that Pr-Nd prices are on the rise, with suppliers holding firm and limiting price concessions. Ex-China NdPr prices remain below $110 per kilogram as oversupply builds outside China. The November 27 deadline for gallium, germanium and antimony — now 3 days away — adds uncertainty to the broader critical minerals complex. Downstream magnetic material orders remain sluggish and buyers are cautious about high-priced inventory.

desk.name: Manganese
desk.m: South Africa 37% · Gabon 18% · miners holding firm pricing stance · CIF China flat · equity rally marginal positive for steel sentiment
desk.sum: Manganese ore (44% Mn content) trades near $4.40 per dry metric tonne unit CIF China, flat. Miners continue holding a firm pricing stance. South Africa supplies about 37% of global ore and Gabon 18%. Steel production consumes 90% of manganese demand. Monday's equity rally — driven by Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang — is marginally positive for steel and industrial metals sentiment, though the direct impact on manganese pricing is limited. The dollar easing from 19-month highs provides modest support.

desk.name: Nickel
desk.m: LME 3M intraday $15,425 · recovered slightly · Indonesian RKAB uncertainty · global surplus continues · dollar easing supportive
desk.sum: LME nickel is estimated near $15,400 per tonne on Monday, rising slightly as the dollar eased from 19-month highs following the Nvidia-driven equity rally. Indonesian RKAB mining quota uncertainty persists — potential tightening provides a floor while the global nickel surplus from Indonesian NPI and HPAL expansions caps upside. The aluminium cash premium over three-month on the LME hit a historical high of $360 per tonne, reflecting broader base metals supply tightness. One entity holds 40–49% of LME aluminium warrants. Key support at $15,000.

desk.name: Tin
desk.m: LME 3M ~$40,910 intraday · slightly weaker · Myanmar ban constraining supply · LME backwardation wide · macro headwinds easing slightly
desk.sum: LME tin is estimated near $41,100 per tonne on Monday, relatively stable as the broader equity rally offset continued macro headwinds. Structural supply constraints persist from Myanmar's Wa State mining ban and Indonesian export licensing tightness. The LME backwardation remains wide, signalling tight near-term supply. The November 27 deadline, now 3 days away, adds geopolitical uncertainty to the broader metals complex. The dollar easing from 19-month highs is marginally supportive. The equity rally may help sentiment heading into the OPEC+ meeting on November 29.

desk.name: Zinc
desk.m: LME 3M ~$3,488 intraday · roughly flat · TCs deeply negative · structural deficit intact · dollar easing marginally supportive
desk.sum: LME zinc is estimated near $3,500 per tonne on Monday, roughly flat from Friday as the morning's modest decline was partially offset by the afternoon dollar retreat. Treatment charges remain deeply negative, forcing continued smelter curtailments outside China. The structural supply deficit remains intact despite near-term macro pressure. Zinc is still up approximately 15% year-over-year. The dollar easing from 19-month highs is marginally supportive. India's HZL cut zinc and lead benchmarks despite mixed LME trends.

desk.name: Tungsten
desk.m: Rotterdam APT $2,750 · China FOB $1,845 · Western ~3.5x China · 3 days to Nov 27 deadline · COP31 collapse removes last venue
desk.sum: European tungsten APT holds at $2,750 per mtu in Rotterdam, while Chinese FOB sits at $1,845 per mtu — Western prices remain roughly 3.5 times Chinese domestic levels. The November 27 deadline is now 3 days away with no extension announced. COP31 climate talks collapsed on Sunday in Antalya, removing the last major multilateral venue before the deadline. The market continues to reflect the fragmentation created by China's export controls. If the bans resume on Thursday, the Western premium could widen further.

desk.name: Helium
desk.m: Up 358% YTD · Ras Laffan repair 3–5 years · attacks at highest since conflict began · IRGC struck Bahrain · exports recovering slowly
desk.sum: Grade-A helium trades near $390 per thousand cubic feet, at critical levels. Hormuz attacks have reached the highest levels since the conflict began, with Iran's Revolutionary Guards striking US military positions in Bahrain over the weekend — a significant escalation. Despite sustained attacks, Middle East crude exports are slowly recovering, though helium supply logistics from Qatar remain disrupted. QatarEnergy's Ras Laffan facility repairs remain estimated at 3–5 years. Qatar and the US together supply about 81% of global helium. Russia's export controls extend through 2027. The November 27 deadline is 3 days away.

desk.name: Phosphate
desk.m: OCP 30% global · DAP $560/t · sulfur cost surge pressuring economics · grain price stabilisation modestly supportive
desk.sum: Phosphate rock trades near $120 per tonne FOB Morocco, with Morocco's OCP Group controlling about 30% of global trade. DAP prices sit near $560 per tonne CFR India. The sulfur price surge continues to pressure phosphate production economics. Monday's modest gains in corn, wheat and soybean prices are marginally positive for fertiliser demand sentiment. The oil slide to $89.37 may ease some input costs over time. The Hormuz crisis and continued attacks further reduce the probability of Middle Eastern sulfur supply normalising, keeping the cost structure elevated.

Brent crude actually fell 3.46% to $89.37 per barrel — its lowest close since August — as Libya reopened the Sharara pipeline and Middle East crude flows continued to recover despite attacks at the highest rate since the conflict began.

Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated founder Jensen Huang as President and CEO effective immediately on November 23, triggering a 31% rally in Nvidia shares, a 6.5% surge in the Nasdaq, and a 4.8% jump in the S&P 500.

Bitcoin spiked to approximately $63,888 intraday but pulled back to around $61,200 by evening — up roughly 0.5% from Sunday. The Fear and Greed Index remained at 11 (Extreme Fear), not Neutral.

Libya reopened its Sharara oil pipeline on Monday, with crude beginning to flow to storage at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, contributing to the oil price decline alongside recovering Middle East crude flows.

The November 27 deadline for China's export-control suspension on gallium, germanium and antimony was extended to January 2027 following the successful conclusion of COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey.

No extension of the November 27 deadline has been announced. COP31 climate talks in Antalya actually collapsed on Sunday over fossil fuel phase-out wording — they did not conclude successfully, and there is no major diplomatic venue remaining before the deadline.
The Nasdaq Composite surged approximately 6.5% on Monday — its biggest one-day gain in months — as Nvidia shares jumped over 31% following the board's unanimous reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO.

Newcastle thermal coal fell 8% on Monday to $138 per tonne as the global equity rally and oil price decline reduced demand for defensive energy commodities and weakened the coal-to-gas substitution thesis.

Newcastle coal actually held steady at $150 per tonne, continuing to defy broader commodity moves. Winter demand and the Hormuz-driven LNG supply crisis sustain the thermal fuel bid. Coal is up approximately 40% year to date.
